Wind & Data Infrastructure

IBEW and the IBEW/NECA JATC, IUOE, the Ironworkers and their IMPACT programme, the UA and SMART as training bodies

Programme completion record; the credentials it rehearses are issued only by their own bodies — 29 CFR 1910.269 and 29 CFR 1910.147 for the turbine, the substation and the hall, NFPA 70E for every absence-of-voltage test, ANSI Z359 for the tower and the platform, NFPA 70 (NEC) and BICSI practice for the busway and the pathway; every height, wind, voltage, torque, load, depth and limit lives in the manufacturer's manual, the switching order, the lift plan or the dive plan

Eight jobs across a ridge wind farm, a data hall under construction and an ocean data pod: the climb proven on the ground, the nacelle locked and its yaw held, the blade platform's wind go/no-go, collector switching to a written order, a busway torqued and signed, one floor tile out and attended, a CRAH alarm answered in a live hall, and a sealed pod landed and isolated before its hatch opens. Each station runs with a declared ?fault= that changes the scene and one step's right answer, and no figure is ever stated — the manual, the order and the plans hold them.

Every level reaches 75 lessons. A lesson is one station step run under one condition; each level's number is its tasks' steps added up from the station modules.

The ladder

Level 1 is open; each level opens when the one below is passed — every task in one run of it a mastery run. A task opens its station with its condition; the number after each task is its steps.

Energy & Power

Turbine Climb & Rescue-Kit Check

12 steps · 4 hazards · 2 interruptions · par 5 min

The climb is decided on the ground: the wind read against the site's limit, the harness walked by hand, the rescue kit opened and a second climber confirmed before the runner goes on the rail.

  • ANSI/ASSP — ANSI/ASSP Z359 — Fall Protection Code

  • union — Ironworkers and IMPACT — apprenticeship and safety training for structural, ornamental and reinforcing ironwork
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.23 — Ladders
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.269 — Electric power generation, transmission and distribution
  • OSHA — 29 CFR 1910.28 — Duty to have fall protection and falling object protection

What it proves

Competency: Climb, lock out, switch, torque, open a floor, answer an alarm and land a pod across a wind farm, a data hall and an ocean data centre without stating a figure the manual or the plan holds

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 4 of its 8 stations, against OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269 — Electric power generation, transmission and distribution; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.147 The control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout); NFPA 70E Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace; ANSI/ASSP Z359 Fall Protection Code; NEC/NFPA 70 NFPA 70 — National Electrical Code; BICSI BICSI Installer 2 and Optical Fiber installer credentials.

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: Programme completion record; the credentials it rehearses are issued only by their own bodies — 29 CFR 1910.269 and 29 CFR 1910.147 for the turbine, the substation and the hall, NFPA 70E for every absence-of-voltage test, ANSI Z359 for the tower and the platform, NFPA 70 (NEC) and BICSI practice for the busway and the pathway; every height, wind, voltage, torque, load, depth and limit lives in the manufacturer's manual, the switching order, the lift plan or the dive plan. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
